gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the total cost of a working two-PC, two-monitor DisplayPort setup once you add the DP cables each box leaves out (six are needed). AV Access 8KSW21DP-DM comes to $159.99 total because all six are in the box. CKL 622DP-4 comes to $175.99 because it is missing two. Level1Techs comes to $598 because it ships with none.
standout_why: I read the full lists from the cited TESmart DKS202-M24 page (its URL returned HTTP 429 every time, so I could not read its body) and the Level1Techs store page, plus the top organic results gearexplained.com/guides/dual-monitor-kvm-switch and dockgearhq.com/blog/best-kvm-switches-for-dual-monitor-setups-2026. GearExplained notes that the AV Access 8KSW21DP-DM includes six DP cables, but it lists no prices and covers no CKL, ATEN or Level1Techs cable counts. DockGearHQ counts 'six host-side cables' per setup but gives no prices and only says Level1Techs cabling is 'not bundled'. ChatGPT's own cards ($149.99 CKL, $329.90 TESmart, $555.26 StarTech) are bare switch prices. None of these pages adds the missing cables to reach a total cost.
decides: The order changes once cables are counted. The AV Access 8KSW21DP-DM ($159.99, six DP 1.4a cables included, rated to 4K 144/165 Hz) becomes the cheapest complete setup, below the CKL card ChatGPT showed as the budget pick ($149.99 + 2 missing monitor cables ≈ $175.99). Level1Techs ($520 + 6 × $13 = $598) costs more than ChatGPT's 'premium' StarTech card price. Neither AV Access nor CKL supports EDID emulation, so a shopper who needs EDID still has to pay for the TESmart, Level1Techs or another higher-priced switch. AV Access is already a Dealectric program (awin:avaccess), but the 8KSW21DP-DM itself is not listed yet.
